before.known: I know an old man who wanted to ask for help
before.target: 我认识一个老男人，他以前想请求帮助

decisions.why: 老男人 'old male-person' is not how Chinese says 'an old man' — it sounds crude ('old geezer'). The course's own later LEGO is 老人 'an old man / old person' (S0264L01). Seed + LEGO edit → held.
decisions.gloss: 老 old · 男人 man (male person)

decisions.why: Second Chinese for 'woman': S0229L01 teaches 'woman | 女人', this LEGO teaches 'woman | 妇人' (妇人 is old-fashioned/literary). Exact ZUT clash: S0230L01U02 'do you know that woman? | 你认识那个女人吗？' vs S0232L01U04 'do you know that woman? | 你认识那个妇人吗'. 老妇人 'old woman' (S0232L02) is fine as a whole chunk; the bare 'woman | 妇人' LEGO is the problem. Never delete a LEGO: options are to grow it to 'old woman | 老妇人' (merge with L02) or give it a distinct English (e.g. 'lady').
decisions.gloss: 妇人 fùrén — woman (literary/old-fashioned)

decisions.why: ZUT at LEGO level: 'my mother' is taught as 我妈 (S0181L02B01 'my mother | 我妈') and again here as 我妈妈. Both are correct Chinese (妈 is more colloquial), but the same English now has two answers across the course. Kai's call which one 'my mother' maps to.
decisions.gloss: 我妈妈 wǒ māma my mum · 我妈 wǒ mā my mum (colloquial)

decisions.why: ZUT at LEGO level: 'my father' is 我爸爸 (S0240L01B02) and here 我父亲 (formal 'father'). Same English, two answers (e.g. S0240L01U11 'you must tell my father | 你必须告诉我爸爸' vs S0266L01U03 'do you know my father? | 你认识我父亲吗？'). Seed 266 'an old friend of my father' is fine either way. Kai's call.
decisions.gloss: 我父亲 wǒ fùqīn my father (formal) · 我爸爸 wǒ bàba my dad

decisions.gloss: 我觉得 I think · 那是个 that is a · 好想法 good idea/thought

decisions.why: 会说得(很)好 mixes 会 'can / will' with the manner complement 说得好 'speaks well'. As written it reads 'she will speak (very) well' (a prediction), not 'she speaks well'. Natural: 她(中文)说得很好.
